carrots-frozen-cooked-with-butter-or-mar.title: Carrots, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Carrots, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine are a ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh carrots that are quickly frozen after being briefly cooked with butter or margarine. The process preserves the bright colour, tender texture and natural sweetness of the carrot.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezing retains most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh carrots.
Cooking with butter or margarine enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K.
Frozen carrots are a staple ingredient in many mixed vegetable side dishes and soups.
Heat treatment softens the carrots, making them easier for children and seniors to eat.
Butter adds a richer aroma, while margarine extends shelf life.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fibre in carrots promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: Butter‑cooked versions may trigger reactions in people sensitive to milk proteins or lactose.

items.title: Higher fat content
items.content: Added butter increases the calorie density; portion control is advisable for weight‑watchers.

items.title: Sodium in margarine
items.content: Some margarines contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the carrots in a skillet, microwave, or steamer. They work well as a side dish for meat or fish, in vegetable stews, soups, and salads. Finish with fresh herbs, spices, or a squeeze of lemon for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen carrots in an airtight bag at –18 °C. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and store in a sealed container in the refrigerator. Do not refreeze.

content.title: About
content.content: Lemon pie filling is a ready‑to‑use filling made from lemon juice, sugar, eggs and starch, designed for quick preparation of lemon pies and tarts. It has a bright sweet‑tart flavor, smooth creamy texture and a pale yellow color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The filling is a key component of the classic American Key Lime Pie.
Recipes often include real lemon juice and zest for authentic aroma.
Starch such as corn starch or pectin is added to stabilize the texture.
It can be used beyond pies, for example as a filling for cupcakes, profiteroles or dessert sandwiches.
Gluten‑free versions replace wheat starch with potato or tapioca starch.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Lemon juice provides vitamin C, an antioxidant that supports the immune system.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity of lemon can stimulate gastric juice production, helping digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The filling typically contains no added fats, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Lemons supply potassium, which is important for blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Natural antibacterial properties
items.content: Lemon juice has mild antibacterial effects that help preserve freshness.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to lemons.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The product contains added sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain commercial versions may contain preservatives; choose preservative‑free options if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Pour the filling into a pre‑baked crust and bake until set, or chill it and use as a cold filling. It pairs well with meringue, whipped cream and fresh berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container for up to 7 days. Once opened, consume within 3‑4 days. Discard if off‑smell or color changes.

potato-roasted-from-fresh-peel-not-eaten.title: Potato, roasted, fresh, peel not eaten, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato is a whole tuber cooked in the oven without added fat. The peel is not consumed, leaving only the flesh and its natural nutrients. This cooking method preserves most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh potatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 8,000 years.
Roasting brings out a natural sweetness through caramelization of sugars.
Without the peel, roasted potatoes are easier to digest for people with sensitive stomachs.
Roasted potatoes are often used as a base for healthy side dishes and diet meals.
Compared with fried potatoes, roasted potatoes contain far fewer calories and fat.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes roasted potatoes suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: If tubers are damaged or sprouting, solanine levels can rise; such parts should be removed.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Roasted potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted potatoes are served as a side dish, diced into salads, used in casseroles, or enjoyed as a simple snack, seasoned with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh potatoes in a cool, dark place at 4–10 °C. After roasting, let them cool, then keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Quesadilla with egg and meat is a Mexican dish consisting of a thin corn or wheat tortilla filled with scrambled egg and sautéed meat (usually beef or chicken). It is quick to prepare, filling, and rich in protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The quesadilla originated in central Mexico as a convenient way to use leftover meat and eggs.
Traditionally cheese is added, but in the egg‑and‑meat version cheese is often omitted or used sparingly.
The dish is popular at street stalls and fast‑food outlets because it can be assembled and cooked in minutes.
In the United States quesadillas are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs and meat provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat are abundant in B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: When made with corn tortillas the carbohydrate load remains moderate, fitting low‑carb diets.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Meat provides zinc, important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Fatty cuts of meat can raise cholesterol levels, so lean options are recommended.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to egg whites and should avoid the dish.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If sauces or pre‑made seasonings are added, the sodium level may become high.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Meat must be fully cooked and eggs cooked until firm to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quesadilla is conveniently eaten by hand, cut into wedges. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or a squeeze of fresh lime. Add fresh veggies such as tomatoes, avocado, or lettuce for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared quesadilla in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave to restore a crisp crust.
